items.title: Fed Watches Inflation Picture Turn Uglier | Charles Schwab
items.excerpt: November 23, 2026• Henry Hoenig In late October, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said policymakers wanted more information before agreeing to raise interest rates again. At least some of what they've seen hasn't been pretty. Yes, the rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) decelerated from 0.6% month over month in September to 0.4% in October. But energy accounted for 58% of September's rise, while in October it accounted for only 15%, making energy a relatively minor factor in the latest reading. Still, October's gain works out to annualized inflation of about 4.3%. Zooming out also reveals a less-than-attractive picture. Over the three months through October, CPI rose an annualized 5.7%, while the wholesale Producer Price Index (PPI) for final demand rose an annualized 9%. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose at a 3.7% annualized rate during the same period. That's more than double the 1.6% pace it set in the three months through July. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price data for October is due November 25. PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. But Fed Governor Christopher J. Waller didn't wait for it. Hours before the CPI release on November 10, he said that if October CPI rose 0.3% or more, the Fed should consider raising rates by a half percentage point at its December meeting to maintain its inflation-fighting credibility. Waller, who voted to hold rates steady in October, noted particular concern about the breadth of price increases. ## Inflation spreads? Inflation appears to be spreading. In October, 105 of 177 CPI expenditure categories (59%) rose faster than a 3% annualized rate. That equals the highest level since August 2022, up from 49% in September and 46% in August. In all, 27 categories rose the most in at least a year, including household furnishings and supplies (up 0.7% month over month), motor vehicle insurance (up 0.7%), and club memberships and sports fees (up 1.2%). Several regional Fed gauges that track the underlying inflation trend have turned up again, reaching the highest levels since May. The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's core sticky-price index, which excludes food and energy and tracks slower-moving items, rose at a one-month annualized rate of 4.7% in October. ... But in a November 10 speech, Waller cited Fed staff research indicating that energy prices may drive goods and services prices for longer than they did in the pre-pandemic era, possibly well into 2027, especially if oil prices remain elevated. Oil and gasoline prices have fallen somewhat, and that'll help. But global refinery constraints have caused diesel prices to diverge somewhat from oil prices, and diesel feeds into inflation via more channels than gasoline does. Diesel powers the trucks that deliver goods and the farm machinery used to grow food. As of November 16, diesel prices were down only 9% from their record high set in September, compared to a 22% decline for WTI crude oil from its October high. October's PPI data showed that truck freight rates rose 3.9% from a month earlier and 25% from a year earlier, while wholesale food prices rose 1.3% from a month earlier, the fastest increase since February.

items.title: Headline PCE inflation has run above core for seven months, by 0.5 point in September | FinanceInTime
items.excerpt: US inflation as the Federal Reserve targets it, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, has run above its core measure in each of the seven months from March through September, after trailing it in January and February, according to index data compiled by the St. Louis Fed from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In September the 12-month rate was 3.6%, against 3.1% excluding food and energy, a gap of 0.5 percentage point. ... ## What the officials say is behind it New York Fed President John C. Williams said on November 23 that inflation is "about 3-1/2 percent" and named three drivers: higher tariffs on imported goods, supply-chain disruption and higher energy prices linked to conflicts in the Middle East, and strong demand for goods tied to AI investment. He said "the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and severe capacity constraints in oil refining" have pushed up crude oil prices and the spreads of gasoline and diesel over crude, as FinanceInTime reported. Governor Lisa D. Cook said in a November 20 speech that the 12-month change in the PCE price index was estimated at 3.8% in October and the core measure at 3.2%, a gap of 0.6 percentage point (computed). She added that the core measure "underscores that, while energy is a significant contributor to inflation, the sources of price pressure facing American families are increasingly varied." Williams and Cook therefore describe different parts of the same picture: Williams places energy and AI-related goods at the center, and Cook points to core prices that show pressure beyond energy. ... The FRED series are index levels for the headline and core measures. They do not split the headline into energy, food and other components, so they do not show how much of the gap in any month is energy. The data also do not show why the order reversed in March; the explanations above are the officials' own and are attributed to them. October's figures are estimates, and BEA's own release is still to come.

items.title: Daily Brew: November 24, 2026 - Ballotpedia
items.excerpt: The nine states that used new Congressional maps in this year's general election are on track to send 16 to 18 more Democrats to Washington than they did in the last Congress, even though the states enacted new maps that included a net of nine new Republican-leaning districts that President Donald Trump (R) would have won in the 2024 presidential election. As of Nov. 23, Democrats have netted 17 seats in the eight states other than Louisiana. Louisiana’s two Dec. 12 general elections will decide whether the final total is 16, 17, or 18. One common way to measure how a map may favor one party is to compare districts by how their voters cast ballots for president in recent elections. Because most of the new districts did not exist in 2024, this comparison uses 2024 presidential results recalculated for the 2026 boundaries, not votes actually cast in those districts. By that measure, Democrats won 26 districts across those states that Trump would have won, and Republicans did not win any districts that Kamala Harris (D) would have won. Those figures could change because both Louisiana general elections are in Trump-won districts. The total could still shift depending on how Louisiana voters decide races for the 5th and 6th Congressional Districts — each between a Democrat and a Republican — on Dec. 12. Before the election, Louisiana’s six-member delegation had four Republicans and two Democrats. Of the four seats already decided under the new map, Republicans won three and Democrats won one. If the parties split the runoffs, Louisiana’s balance will hold and the nine-state net gain will be 17. If Democrats win both, it will be 18. If Republicans win both, it will be 16.

items.title: What could Democrats do with their expanding congressional majority? | Politics News | Al Jazeera
items.excerpt: The Democratic Party has continued to expand its already sizeable majorities in the United States Congress as counting concludes in the final races of the 2026 midterm elections. As of Monday, the Democrats hold a 258-seat majority in the 435-member House of Representatives. Four races remain uncalled. All the races have been decided, meanwhile, for the Senate, where Democrats gained a 56-seat majority out of 100 total seats. Flipping both chambers gives the party a strong hand to shape legislation during the last two years of Trump’s term in office. How might the Democrats approach their role in government once the new Congress is sworn in on January 3? ... ## What do the results say? The midterm results give Democrats their largest House majority since 1992 and their largest Senate majority in more than a decade. Republicans, meanwhile, saw their tally in the House drop to 173 seats, their lowest figure in years. The vote also served as a firm rebuke of Trump’s second term as president, with voters venting their frustration over cost-of-living issues, the US-Israel war on Iran, aggressive immigration raids and corruption. Democratic victories also extended well beyond traditional left-wing strongholds, with candidates racking up wins in Republican-led states such as Texas, Mississippi and South Carolina. ... Four House seats have yet to be called: one in Minnesota, one in Tennessee, and two in Louisiana that will be settled by a run-off on December 12. Those races could see the Democrats further expand their majority in the House. The final count is now a question of just how large the party’s ... ## What will Democrats do with their majority? Democrats have long pledged to use any congressional majorities they win as a check on Trump’s agenda. But the scale of their success in the 2026 midterms has prompted discussion about embracing a more ambitious legislative agenda. In the House of Representatives, Democrats have outlined a 100-day agenda that includes potentially reversing tax cuts that largely benefit wealthy earners and restoring healthcare subsidies that expired under Trump. Lawmakers have also said that they will act to end the war on Iran, although divisions remain within the party over how to rein in Trump’s military actions. Under the US Constitution, Congress alone can authorise military operations. Progressives have accused the party’s moderate wing of playing down expectations of firm steps to end the war, including cutting off funding. Democrats have also pledged to use their newfound position to exercise oversight over the executive branch by launching probes and issuing subpoenas. On Monday, for example, House Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries said that a Democrat-led Congress would conduct a “swift, thorough, and wide-ranging” investigation into the actions of the chip manufacturer Nvidia. He also said it would delve into the “corrupt abuse of power” by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. In the Senate, Democrats have also threatened to block Trump’s nominees for high-level government positions, which require the chamber’s confirmation. ## What role will Trump play? While Democrats will hold substantial majorities in both chambers of Congress, Trump will retain the power to veto legislation. ... There is little evidence, however, to suggest that Trump is planning a political pivot after the midterms. Within a week of the vote, for instance, Trump named Stephen Miller — one of the architects of his hardline policies on immigration — as White House chief of staff. The staffing shake-up was seen as a doubling-down on right-wing policy priorities. While Trump has, at times, suggested that he could cooperate with Democratic lawmakers, he has also promised to use his veto power aggressively.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 24 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: ## Lead stories Home Alone sequel in early development with Macaulay Culkin returning. Macaulay Culkin is set to return as Kevin McCallister in a new Home Alone sequel in early development at 20th Century Studios. Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg are writing and producing through Point Grey, working from Culkin’s own pitch, Entertainment Weekly reports, citing Deadline. Kevin is now a father, locked out of his own home by his son. No director, further cast or release date has been announced, and Disney declined to comment, The Daily Star reports. Avengers: Doomsday to skip early awards screenings. Avengers: Doomsday will skip early awards screenings to protect spoilers, per Variety, via Mezha. The decision leaves the film out of the Critics Choice, Golden Globe and BAFTA races, because voting in all three closes before its 18 December 2026 release. The Actor Awards remain possible, with voting falling after the film opens. Blade Runner 2099 releases three new sneak peeks. Three new sneak peeks from Blade Runner 2099 put Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer at the centre of the run-up, one day ahead of the series premiere. Prime Video says all eight episodes arrive on 25 November 2026, following the final-trailer breakdown SvcZZ already published. ... K-POP: The Debut trailer out. Paramount has released the official trailer for K-POP: The Debut, with Ji-young Yoo as aspiring idol Lizzy Lee, Eric Nam and Tony Revolori alongside her. Benson Lee directs, ComingSoon reports, and the film reaches cinemas on 26 February 2027. Mr. Irrelevant trailer out. David Corenswet plays John Tuggle, the last pick of the 1983 NFL draft, in the trailer for Mr. Irrelevant. Michael Shannon plays Giants coach Bill Parcells, ComingSoon reports, and Jonathan Levine directs. The film reaches cinemas on 25 December 2026. Hello Kadhal trailer out. The official trailer for Hello Kadhal is out, with Arya in his 40th film as lead alongside Nikhila Vimal and Vaishnavi Chaitanya, and the film reaches cinemas on 4 December 2026, Filmibeat reports. Nikhil Muraly directs, SPI Music reports on YouTube. Merry Boys trailer out. The trailer for Merry Boys, a Malayalam campus entertainer starring Aishwarya Raj, is out. Mahesh Manas directs, Mathrubhumi English reports. It reaches theatres in December 2026, with no exact date announced. Monkey King trailer out. The Chinese animated film Monkey King has unveiled a new trailer, and Malay Mail reports it reaches Chinese cinemas on 5 December 2026. Ariana Grande announces an Eternal Sunshine tour film for Peacock. Ariana Grande has announced an Eternal Sunshine tour film for Peacock, with a teaser out on 23 November 2026. No release date has been announced, ComingSoon reports, and the format, documentary or concert film, is unconfirmed. The Trust trailer out ahead of its Netflix premiere. Netflix has released the trailer for The Trust, a documentary pairing Idris Elba with King Charles III to mark 50 years of The King’s Trust. It premieres globally on Netflix on 26 December 2026, What’s on Netflix reports. ... Crave renews Yaga for season 2. Crave has renewed mystery thriller Yaga for a second season, with Carrie-Anne Moss returning. The season 1 finale airs on 27 November 2026, KZK101 reports, and no premiere date has been announced for season 2.

items.title: Qatar’s Film Committee announces Mohamed Mounir music biopic celebrating his life, legacy | The Peninsula Qatar
items.excerpt: Published: 24 Nov 2026 - 10:54 am | Last Updated: 24 Nov 2026 - 10:55 am ... Doha, Qatar: The Film Committee at Media City Qatar has announced plans to develop a new music biopic celebrating the life and legacy of Mohamed Mounir (pictured), the legendary Egyptian artist known to millions of fans as “El King”. Announced during the second edition of Doha Industry Days, the feature film will bring Mounir’s remarkable story to the big screen, tracing his journey from beginnings to becoming one of the Arab world’s most celebrated and influential artists, and exploring the experiences, relationships and creative choices that shaped his life and artistic identity. ... The project grants the Film Committee the rights to document Mounir’s life story in collaboration with award-winning partners, including a leading regional studio to produce the feature. Production partners to be announced. Alongside the feature film, plans include a behind-the-scenes documentary featuring interviews with Mounir
